docs.title: What is Fusion?
docs.text: Fusion is a CLI TCG game that lives in your terminal. You can collect and trade cards with other players, as well as the server. We encourage bots that can make trades and buy from the server and auctions.

docs.title: Why choose Fusion?
docs.text:
We know there are lots of TCG's out there, but Fusion is the best choice for a tech-y TCG.

Feature Fusion Others Card numbering uint16_t Arbitrary Card naming Based on card number Arbitrary Theme Tech/Computers Other Encourages bots? Yes No Runs... CLI In the web Has cool docs? Yes No

docs.title: API
docs.text: The API primarily uses GET and POST requests to the same HTTP server that the docs are running on.

docs.title: GET /api/cards.csv
docs.text: Returns a CSV (Comma Separated Value list) of all the cards.

docs.title: GET /api/seasons.csv
docs.text: Returns a CSV (Comma Separated Value list) of all the seasons.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
Fusion cards all have an ID and some have a name. The id's range from 0 to 65535 - the uint16_t limit. Some cards have a name, whilst other's just an id. The name typically corresponds to something relate to the id.

Here are some example cards.

Id Name 0 Stdin 1 Stdout 2 Stderr 3 USB 3.0 4 IPv4 5 Raspberry Pi 5 6 Unix V6 7 Windows 7 8 uint8_t 10 OS-X 16 Base 16 - Hex 21 FTP - Port 21 22 SSH - Port 22 23 Telnet - Port 23 64 Commodore 64 80 HTTP - Port 80 84 TI-84 255 0xFF

docs.title: Currency
docs.text:
Fusion uses a custom currency with multiple different coins.

The coins are:

  • Megons (10 Kilons)
  • Kilons (10 Unons)
  • Unons (10 Milons)
  • Milons (10 Microns)
  • Microns (10 Nanons)
  • Nanons (10 Picons)
  • Picons

Each coin is worth 10 times the previous. I.E. 10 Picons = 1 Nanon, 10 Nanons = 1 Micron, etc.

For comparison, 1 Picon is approximately $0.01 USD and 1 Nanon is $0.10 USD.

NOTE: You CAN NOT buy coins for Fusion and anyone claiming to sell them is likely trying to scam you.

If you do not seee a unit, then assume it is in unons.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Fusion uses many commands to acheive different tasks.

docs.title: help
docs.text: Show the command reference. - help — Prints all available commands

docs.title: whoami
docs.text: Show your current username. - whoami — Prints the logged-in username

docs.title: exit
docs.text: Exit the program. - exit — Closes the client

docs.title: login
docs.text: Login to your account. - login — Prompts for credentials interactively

docs.title: register
docs.text: Register a new account. - register — Prompts for a new username and password

docs.title: logout
docs.text: Logout of your account. - logout — Ends the current session

docs.title: cards [username]
docs.text: Show cards. - cards — Show your own cards - cards alice — Show alice's cards

docs.title: money [username]
docs.text: Show balance. - money — Show your own balance - money alice — Show alice's balance

docs.title: stats [username]
docs.text: Show stats. - stats — Show your own stats - stats alice — Show alice's stats

docs.title: search-cards <query>
docs.text: Search cards by name. - search-cards dragon — Find all cards with "dragon" in the name - search-cards "fire sword" — Exact phrase search

docs.title: search-users <query>
docs.text: Search users by username. - search-users ali — Find users whose name contains "ali"

docs.title: search-seasons <query>
docs.text: Search seasons by name. - search-seasons winter — Find seasons matching "winter"

docs.title: token [+|-|list|get] [name]
docs.text: Manage auth tokens. - token list — List all saved tokens - token + mytoken — Create a new token named "mytoken" - token - mytoken — Delete the token named "mytoken" - token get mytoken — Print the value of "mytoken"

docs.title: servers [+|-|list|get] [name]
docs.text: Manage server aliases. - servers list — List all saved servers - servers + prod — Add a server aliased "prod" - servers - prod — Remove the server aliased "prod" - servers get prod — Print the URL for "prod"

docs.title: connect-chat <url|name> [token]
docs.text: Connect to a chat server. - connect-chat prod — Connect using saved server alias "prod" - connect-chat tcp://localhost:1337 — Connect by URL directly - connect-chat prod mytoken — Connect using alias "prod" and token "mytoken"

docs.title: message <message> [username]
docs.text: Send a chat message. - message hello — Broadcast to all connected users - message hey alice — Send directly to alice

docs.title: chat-console
docs.text:
Enter interactive chat mode. - chat-console — Opens the console — type exit to leave

<required> [optional]

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
You can connect over TCP with Telnet, Netcat or another client.

The server address is localhost:23

docs.title: Connecting with Windows
docs.text:
First, you need to install Telnet. If you already have Telnet installed, you can skip this step.

Open powershell or command prompt and run:

dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient

Then, connect to Fusion:

telnet localhost 23

docs.title: Connecting with Mac
docs.text:
In order to install Telnet, you need a package manager. The standard MacOS package manager is Brew. If you already have Brew installed, you can skip this step (To check, run brew --version).

Open Terminal and run:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

Then to install telnet, run:

brew install telnet

Now, you can connect to Fusion with:

telnet localhost 23

docs.title: Connecting with Linux
docs.text:
In order to install Telnet, you need to install APT, a package manager. You probably already have APT installed.

Note for Chromebook users: You need to install the Linux development environment for the Terminal app to work.

To check, run in your Terminal:

apt --version

If the command succeeds, then you can proceed to the next step (Using APT).

Then, install telnet with APT.

apt install telnet

You can now connect to Fusion with:

telnet localhost 23
